claim: Nuclear Export Factor 2 (Nxf2) and its co-factor, Nxt1, form a complex with Panoramix (Panx) and are required for co-transcriptional silencing of transposons in somatic and germline cells of the ovary.
source: Here we show that Nuclear Export Factor 2 (Nxf2) and its co-factor, Nxt1, form a complex with Panx and are required for co-transcriptional silencing of transposons in somatic and germline cells of the ovary.
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data showing co-purification of Nxf2, Nxt1, and Panx (Figure 1A, 1D), and by functional data showing transposon de-repression in nxf2 mutants (Figure 1E-G).

claim: Tethering of Nxf2 or Nxt1 to RNA results in silencing of target loci and the concomitant accumulation of repressive chromatin marks.
source: Tethering of Nxf2 or Nxt1 to RNA results in silencing of target loci and the concomitant accumulation of repressive chromatin marks.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing reduced RNA and protein expression from tethering reporters (Figure 4B) and increased H3K9me3 marks (Figure 4C).

claim: Nxf2 and Panx proteins are mutually required for proper localization and stability.
source: Nxf2 and Panx proteins are mutually required for proper localization and stability.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence showing loss of nuclear localization upon knockdown (Figure 2A-B) and western blots showing reduced protein levels in mutants (Figure 2C-D).

claim: The amino-terminal portion of Panx is sufficient to induce transcriptional silencing.
source: We mapped the protein domains crucial for the Nxf2/Panx complex formation and show that the amino-terminal portion of Panx is sufficient to induce transcriptional silencing.
evidence: Supported by DNA tethering experiments showing that LacI-Panx-ΔC (lacking C-terminus) can still silence reporters (Figure 4G).

claim: Three proteins showed the strongest enrichment and significance in GFP-Panx immunoprecipitation: Panx, Nxf2 and Nxt1.
source: Three proteins showed the strongest enrichment and significance: Panx, Nxf2 and Nxt1 (Figure 1A, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by quantitative mass spectrometry data from GFP-Panx immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Nxf2 is a homolog of the general messenger RNA (mRNA) export factor Nxf1 but was reported previously as being dispensable for canonical mRNA transport in S2 cells.
source: Nxf2 is a homolog of the general messenger RNA (mRNA) export factor Nxf1 but was reported previously as being dispensable for canonical mRNA transport in S2 cells (Herold et al., 2001; Herold et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies by Herold et al.

claim: Nxf2 contains all domains present in the family defined by Nxf1, namely an amino-terminal region (NTR), an RNA-binding domain (RBD), leucine-rich repeats (LRR), the NTF2-like domain (NTF2) and a Ubiquitin-associated (UBA) domain.
source: Nxf2 contains all domains present in the family defined by Nxf1, namely an amino-terminal region (NTR), an RNA-binding domain (RBD), leucine-rich repeats (LRR), the NTF2-like domain (NTF2) and a Ubiquitin-associated (UBA) domain (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) (Herold et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by domain structure diagram (Figure 1B) and citation to Herold et al., 2001.

claim: Nxt1, also known as p15, is a co-factor of Nxf1 responsible for interaction with the Nuclear Pore Complex (NPC), specifically through the NTF2-fold.
source: Nxt1, also known as p15, is a co-factor of Nxf1 responsible for interaction with the NPC, specifically through the NTF2-fold (Fribourg et al., 2001; Lévesque et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies by Fribourg et al., 2001 and Lévesque et al., 2001.

claim: Nxt1 was also reported to interact with Nxf2.
source: Interestingly, Nxt1 was also reported to interact with Nxf2 (Herold et al., 2001; Herold et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies by Herold et al.

claim: Both Nxf2 and Nxt1 were previously identified in screens for piRNA-guided silencing in somatic and germline cells, and their depletion resulted in female sterility.
source: Both Nxf2 and Nxt1 were previously identified in screens for piRNA-guided silencing in somatic and germline cells, and their depletion resulted in female sterility (Czech et al., 2013; Handler et al., 2013; Muerdter et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies by Czech et al., 2013, Handler et al., 2013, and Muerdter et al., 2013.

claim: No enrichment for Piwi was detected by mass spectrometry in GFP-Panx immunoprecipitation.
source: Contrary to expectations based upon previous findings (Sienski et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2015), we saw no enrichment for Piwi by mass spectrometry (Figure 1A), results that are consistent with another recent study (Batki et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data (Figure 1A) and citation to Batki et al., 2019.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments detected weak but reproducible interactions between Piwi and Panx, Nxf2, and Nxt1.
source: However, co-immunoprecipitation experiments detected weak but reproducible interactions between Piwi and Panx, Nxf2, and Nxt1, but not with a negative control (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: GFP-Nxf2 is expressed in follicle and germline cells of the ovary and localizes predominantly to nuclei.
source: GFP-Nxf2 is expressed in follicle and germline cells of the ovary and localizes predominantly to nuclei (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images showing GFP-Nxf2 localization (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).

claim: Mass spectrometry of GFP-Nxf2-associated proteins identified Panx, Nxf2, and Nxt1, as binding partners.
source: Mass spectrometry of GFP-Nxf2-associated proteins identified Panx, Nxf2, and Nxt1, as binding partners (Figure 1D, Figure 1—source data 2)
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data from GFP-Nxf2 immunoprecipitation (Figure 1D).

claim: Trans-heterozygous nxf2 mutants were female sterile, with fewer eggs laid and none hatching.
source: Trans-heterozygous mutants were female sterile, with fewer eggs laid and none hatching (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Supported by egg hatching rate data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: nxf2 mutants were severely compromised in the repression of soma- and germline-specific transposons, in a highly similar manner to panx mutants.
source: nxf2 mutants were severely compromised in the repression of soma- and germline-specific transposons, in a highly similar manner to panx mutants (Figure 1E)
evidence: Supported by qPCR data showing transposon de-repression in nxf2 and panx mutants (Figure 1E).

claim: nxf2 mutants showed no change in piRNA levels or Piwi localization, despite compromised silencing.
source: with no change in piRNA levels or Piwi localization, despite compromised silencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–H).
evidence: Supported by small RNA-seq data (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G) and immunofluorescence images (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).

claim: The expression of protein-coding genes was not generally affected in nxf2 mutants, with only 16 out of 7252 (r2 = 0.963) being changed more than 4-fold.
source: As reported previously, the expression of protein-coding genes was not generally affected in nxf2 mutants, with only 16 out of 7252 (r2 = 0.963) being changed more than 4-fold (Figure 1F) (Herold et al., 2001; Herold et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data (Figure 1F) and citations to previous studies by Herold et al.

claim: 28 out of 60 transposon families (that were above the expression threshold of 1 rpm) were de-repressed by more than 4-fold in nxf2 mutants.
source: In contrast, 28 out of 60 transposon families (that were above the expression threshold of 1 rpm) were de-repressed by more than 4-fold in nxf2 mutants.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis from nxf2 mutant ovaries.

claim: In panx mutants, 16 out of 60 transposons were de-repressed and only 6 out of 7252 genes mis-regulated (r2 = 0.991).
source: Similar results were obtained for panx mutants: 16 out of 60 transposons were de-repressed and only 6 out of 7252 genes mis-regulated (r2 = 0.991).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis from panx mutant ovaries.

claim: ChIP-seq for the H3K9me3 mark from nxf2 mutant ovaries showed reduced methylation levels at the same transposon families that were de-repressed according to RNA-seq.
source: ChIP-seq for the H3K9me3 mark from nxf2 mutant ovaries showed reduced methylation levels at the same transposon families that were de-repressed according to RNA-seq, such as Het-A, while randomly chosen genomic intervals were not changed (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: Supported by H3K9me3 ChIP-seq data from nxf2 mutant ovaries (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B).

claim: RNA-seq from OSCs depleted of Piwi, Panx or Nxf2 showed marked de-repression of soma-specific (e.g. mdg1, gypsy, 297) and intermediate transposon families (e.g. blood) when compared to control cells treated with GFP siRNAs.
source: RNA-seq from OSCs depleted of Piwi, Panx or Nxf2 showed marked de-repression of soma-specific (e.g. mdg1, gypsy, 297) and intermediate transposon families (e.g. blood) when compared to control cells treated with GFP siRNAs (Figure 1G left; Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data from OSCs with knockdowns (Figure 1G left; Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).

claim: The de-repression of transposon families strongly correlates with the reduction in H3K9me3 levels mapped over their consensus sequences in ChIP-seq samples generated from the same knockdowns.
source: The de-repression of transposon families strongly correlates with the reduction in H3K9me3 levels mapped over their consensus sequences in ChIP-seq samples generated from the same knockdowns (Figure 1G right).
evidence: Supported by H3K9me3 ChIP-seq data from OSCs with knockdowns (Figure 1G right).

claim: Piwi depletion resulted in the accumulation of H3K4me2 at Piwi-regulated genomic transposon insertions and spreading of the mark beyond the transposon into downstream regions.
source: Piwi depletion resulted in the accumulation of H3K4me2 at these loci and spreading of the mark, indicative of active transcription, beyond the transposon into downstream regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D,F), similar to earlier reports (Dönertas et al., 2013; Klenov et al., 2014; Sienski et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by H3K4me2 ChIP-seq data from OSCs with Piwi knockdown (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D,F) and citations to previous studies.

claim: Knockdown of panx or nxf2 showed similar, though less pronounced, effects on H3K4me2 accumulation compared to Piwi depletion.
source: Knockdown of panx or nxf2 showed similar, though less pronounced, effects.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of H3K4me2 ChIP-seq data across different knockdowns.

claim: H3K9me3 marks were strongly reduced upon Piwi depletion, with panx and nxf2 knockdowns showing a similar but milder impact.
source: H3K9me3 marks were strongly reduced upon Piwi depletion, with panx and nxf2 knockdowns showing a similar but milder impact (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E,G).
evidence: Supported by H3K9me3 ChIP-seq data from OSCs with knockdowns (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E,G).

claim: Germline knockdown of piwi had no effect on the localization of either Nxf2 or Panx.
source: Germline knockdown of piwi had no effect on the localization of either Nxf2 or Panx.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data from germline-specific knockdowns.

claim: Depletion of Panx led to a pronounced loss of nuclear GFP-Nxf2 in nurse cell nuclei.
source: Depletion of Panx, however, led to a pronounced loss of nuclear GFP-Nxf2 in nurse cell nuclei (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images showing reduced GFP-Nxf2 signal upon Panx knockdown (Figure 2A).

claim: GFP-Panx nuclear signal was reduced upon nxf2 knockdown in nurse cells.
source: The reciprocal was also true, with GFP-Panx nuclear signal being reduced upon nxf2 knockdown in nurse cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images showing reduced GFP-Panx signal upon Nxf2 knockdown (Figure 2B).

claim: Individual depletion of Panx or Nxf2 in follicle cells resulted in a reduction of both proteins.
source: Similarly, the individual depletion of Panx or Nxf2 in follicle cells resulted in a reduction of both proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data from follicle cell-specific knockdowns (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).

claim: Panx protein level was strongly reduced in nxf2 mutant ovaries.
source: Panx protein level was strongly reduced in nxf2 mutant ovaries (Figure 2C)
evidence: Supported by western blot data showing reduced Panx protein in nxf2 mutants (Figure 2C).

claim: GFP-Nxf2 signal was completely lost in homozygous panx mutants.
source: and GFP-Nxf2 signal was completely lost in homozygous panx mutants (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by western blot data showing loss of GFP-Nxf2 protein in panx mutants (Figure 2D).

claim: mRNA levels of Nxf2 and Panx were not affected when the other factor was mutated.
source: Of note, mRNA levels of Nxf2 and Panx were not affected when the other factor was mutated (Figure 1F), implying regulation at the protein level.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data (Figure 1F) showing no change in mRNA levels.

claim: Full-length Nxf2 and Panx robustly co-immunoprecipitated.
source: Full-length Nxf2 and Panx robustly co-immunoprecipitated (Figure 3B)
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data from S2 cells (Figure 3B).

claim: Full-length Nxf2 and Panx co-localized in S2 cell nuclei.
source: and co-localized in S2 cell nuclei (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence images showing co-localization (Figure 3C).

claim: Removing the carboxy-terminal half of Panx (Panx-∆C) yielded a protein that remained nuclear, while co-expressed Nxf2 remained largely cytoplasmic, and these proteins no longer formed a complex.
source: Removing the carboxy-terminal half of Panx (Panx-∆C) yielded a protein that remained nuclear, while co-expressed Nxf2 remained largely cytoplasmic, and these proteins no longer formed a complex (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence data (Figure 3B–D).

claim: When expressed alone in S2 cells, Nxf2 remained predominantly cytoplasmic, suggesting that interaction with Panx is necessary for nuclear localization of Nxf2.
source: When expressed alone in S2 cells, Nxf2 remained predominantly cytoplasmic (ZsGreen-HA in Figure 3C), suggesting that interaction with Panx is necessary for nuclear localization of Nxf2.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data (Figure 3C) showing cytoplasmic localization of Nxf2 alone.

claim: Panx-∆N retained the ability to interact with Nxf2 but failed to localize to the nucleus.
source: Panx-∆N, in contrast, retained the ability to interact with Nxf2 but failed to localize to the nucleus (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence data (Figure 3B–D).

claim: Enforced localization of Panx-∆N to the nucleus also restored nuclear localization of Nxf2.
source: Strikingly, enforced localization of Panx-∆N to the nucleus also restored nuclear localization of Nxf2 (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data showing nuclear localization of Nxf2 with NLS-Panx-∆N (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D).

claim: Deleting only either the coiled coil domain #2 or C-terminal region of Panx reduced co-purification with Nxf2.
source: Deleting only either the coiled coil domain #2 or C-terminal region, which together make up most of the carboxy-terminal half of Panx, reduced co-purification with Nxf2 (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).

claim: Neither Panx-∆CC2 nor Panx-∆CTR constructs were able to rescue mdg1 repression upon panx knockdown.
source: with neither construct being able to rescue mdg1 repression upon panx knockdown (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data from rescue experiments (Figure 3E).

claim: Nxf2-∆NPC failed to co-purify with Panx, and this was accompanied by an increased cytoplasmic protein localization.
source: Nxf2-∆NPC failed to co-purify with Panx, and this was accompanied by an increased cytoplasmic protein localization (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence data (Figure 3B–D).

claim: Deleting the cargo-binding region of Nxf2 had less impact on its co-purification with Panx or the nuclear localization of either protein.
source: In contrast, deleting the cargo-binding region of Nxf2 had less impact on its co-purification with Panx or the nuclear localization of either protein (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence data (Figure 3B–D).

claim: Nxf2-∆Cargo was able to interact with Panx-∆N but not Panx-∆C.
source: This mutant was able to interact with Panx-∆N but not Panx-∆C, as expected (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data (Figure 3F).

claim: Mutants of Nxf2, which had individual domains removed, uniformly failed to rescue nxf2 knockdown in OSCs.
source: Mutants of Nxf2, which had individual domains removed, uniformly failed to rescue nxf2 knockdown in OSCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D)
evidence: Supported by qPCR data from rescue experiments (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).

claim: All Nxf2 domain deletion mutants but Nxf2-∆UBA still co-purified with full-length Panx.
source: yet all but Nxf2-∆UBA still co-purified with full-length Panx (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B–C).

claim: UBA mutant #1 showed reduced binding to Panx, increased cytoplasmic localization, and failure to rescue loss of Nxf2.
source: UBA mutant #1, showed a phenotype similar to the domain deletion with reduced binding to Panx, increased cytoplasmic localization, and failure to rescue loss of Nxf2 (Figure 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–F).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, and rescue experiment data (Figure 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–F).

claim: The interaction of Nxf2 and Panx relies on an intact UBA domain and requires the carboxy-terminal portion of Panx.
source: Thus, the interaction of Nxf2 and Panx relies on an intact UBA domain and requires the carboxy-terminal portion of Panx.
evidence: Inferred from mutational analysis showing loss of interaction when UBA domain or Panx C-terminus is deleted.

claim: All four Nxf2-NTF2 point mutants localized predominantly to the nucleus and co-precipitated quantities of Panx comparable to the full-length control.
source: All four Nxf2-NTF2 point mutants localized predominantly to the nucleus and co-precipitated quantities of Panx comparable to the full-length control (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–F).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and co-immunoprecipitation data (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–F).

claim: Three NTF2 mutants (#1, #2, and #3) failed to rescue transposon de-repression upon depletion of Nxf2.
source: Yet, three mutants (#1, #2, and #3) failed to rescue transposon de-repression upon depletion of Nxf2 (Figure 3E)
evidence: Supported by qPCR data from rescue experiments (Figure 3E).

claim: Reduced amounts of Nxt1 were recovered with the NTF2 mutants #1 and #2.
source: Indeed, reduced amounts of Nxt1 were recovered with the NTF2 mutants #1 and #2, while the NTF2 mutant #4, which rescued transposon expression (Figure 3E), as well as UBA mutants #1 and #2 showed levels comparable to full-length Nxf2 (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data showing Nxt1 binding (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2G).

claim: Expression of λN-Piwi did not lead to reduced RNA or protein levels from the tethering reporter.
source: As expected from previous studies (Sienski et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2015), expression of λN-Piwi did not lead to reduced RNA or protein levels (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from RNA tethering experiments (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and citations to previous studies.

claim: Tethering of λN-Panx resulted in robust repression of sensor RNA and protein signals.
source: Tethering of λN-Panx, in contrast, resulted in robust repression of sensor RNA and protein signals, as reported (Sienski et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from RNA tethering experiments and citations to previous studies.

claim: λN-Nxf2 caused an even stronger reduction of RNA and protein expression from the reporter than λN-Panx.
source: λN-Nxf2 caused an even stronger reduction of RNA and protein expression from the reporter (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from RNA tethering experiments (Figure 4B).

claim: Tethering of λN-Nxt1 induced reporter repression.
source: Tethering of λN-Nxt1 also induced reporter repression (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from RNA tethering experiments (Figure 4B).

claim: Upon tethering of Nxt1, Nxf2 or Panx, increased levels of H3K9me3 were observed over the reporter.
source: Strikingly, upon tethering of Nxt1, Nxf2 or Panx, we observed increased levels of H3K9me3 over the reporter (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by H3K9me3 ChIP-seq data from RNA tethering experiments (Figure 4C).

claim: Nxf2 and Nxt1, along with Panx, act as key effectors of co-transcriptional silencing and are each sufficient to recruit the downstream silencing machinery.
source: These data suggest that Nxf2 and Nxt1, along with Panx, act as key effectors of co-transcriptional silencing and are each sufficient to recruit the downstream silencing machinery.
evidence: Inferred from tethering experiments showing that each factor can induce silencing and H3K9me3 deposition when recruited to RNA.

claim: Tethering of LacI-Piwi did not affect sensor expression in DNA tethering experiments.
source: While tethering of LacI-Piwi did not affect sensor expression, LacI-Panx resulted in robust reductions in both RNA and protein levels (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), as previously reported (Sienski et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from DNA tethering experiments (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D) and citation to previous study.

claim: LacI-Panx resulted in robust reductions in both RNA and protein levels in DNA tethering experiments.
source: While tethering of LacI-Piwi did not affect sensor expression, LacI-Panx resulted in robust reductions in both RNA and protein levels (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), as previously reported (Sienski et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from DNA tethering experiments (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D) and citation to previous study.

claim: LacI-Nxf2 silenced the reporter in DNA tethering experiments, reducing both mRNA and protein output, albeit to a lesser extent than LacI-Panx tethering.
source: LacI-Nxf2 also silenced the reporter, reducing both mRNA and protein output, albeit to a lesser extent than LacI-Panx tethering.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from DNA tethering experiments.

claim: LacI-Nxt1 was unable to silence the sensor construct in DNA tethering experiments.
source: Surprisingly, LacI-Nxt1 was unable to silence the sensor construct.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from DNA tethering experiments.

claim: Repression by tethered Panx or Nxf2 resulted in a striking decrease in H3K4me2 marks over the transcribed parts of the DNA tethering reporter.
source: Repression by tethered Panx or Nxf2 resulted in a striking decrease in H3K4me2 marks over the transcribed parts (i.e. promoter and ZsGreen coding region), while the remainder of the reporter showed low read coverage and little difference in the prevalence of the mark (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by H3K4me2 ChIP-seq data from DNA tethering experiments (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).

claim: H3K9me3 increased upon repression by tethered Panx or Nxf2 in DNA tethering experiments.
source: Conversely, H3K9me3 increased upon repression (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by H3K9me3 ChIP-seq data from DNA tethering experiments (Figure 4F).

claim: The entire reporter sequence (except a small gap around the LacO site and the 3' UTR where the mappability is poor) was prominently decorated with H3K9me3 upon tethering of Panx or Nxf2, suggesting spreading of this chromatin mark following initial silencing.
source: Of note, the entire reporter sequence (except a small gap around the LacO site and the 3' UTR where the mappability is poor) was prominently decorated with H3K9me3, suggesting spreading of this chromatin mark following initial silencing.
evidence: Supported by H3K9me3 ChIP-seq data showing widespread H3K9me3 across the reporter.

claim: Neither LacI-Nxf2-∆Cargo nor LacI-Panx-∆N were able to repress the sensor in DNA tethering experiments.
source: Neither LacI-Nxf2-∆Cargo nor LacI-Panx-∆N, which were predicted to interact with their full-length partner in OSCs (Figure 3B–D), were able to repress the sensor (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from DNA tethering experiments (Figure 4G).

claim: LacI-Panx-∆C substantially reduced RNA and protein expression from the sensor, with its effects as robust as upon DNA tethering of LacI-HP1a.
source: Yet, LacI-Panx-∆C, which could not interact with Nxf2, substantially reduced RNA and protein expression from the sensor, with its effects as robust as upon DNA tethering of LacI-HP1a (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data from DNA tethering experiments (Figure 4G).

claim: The amino-terminal part of Panx is necessary and sufficient to enforce silencing of an artificial reporter independent of its interaction with Nxf2.
source: This suggests that the amino-terminal part of Panx is necessary and sufficient to enforce silencing of an artificial reporter independent of its interaction with Nxf2.
evidence: Inferred from DNA tethering experiments showing that Panx-∆C (lacking C-terminus but retaining N-terminus) can silence reporters without interacting with Nxf2.

claim: Nxf2 and Nxt1 are critical mediators of co-transcriptional gene silencing, acting in concert with Panx to repress loci in response to Piwi-piRNA target engagement.
source: Our data identify Nxf2 and Nxt1 as critical mediators of co-transcriptional gene silencing, acting in concert with Panx to repress loci in response to Piwi-piRNA target engagement (Figure 4H).
evidence: Supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence including mutant analysis, tethering experiments, and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Target recognition by Piwi is necessary to recruit the PICTS complex onto the appropriate nascent RNA targets.
source: The emerging model for piRNA-dependent silencing implies that target recognition by Piwi is necessary to recruit the PICTS complex onto the appropriate nascent RNA targets.
evidence: Inferred from the overall experimental findings and the known role of Piwi in target recognition.

claim: Difficulties in detecting stable interactions between Piwi and PICTS components in vivo may arise from a requirement for Piwi target engagement to licence it for recruitment of silencing complexes.
source: Difficulties in detecting stable interactions between Piwi and PICTS components in vivo may arise from a requirement for Piwi target engagement to licence it for recruitment of silencing complexes, as has been suggested previously (Sienski et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2015).
evidence: Speculative explanation for experimental observations, supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The same mechanism may underlie the difficulties experienced in observing Piwi on its target loci by ChIP.
source: The same mechanism may underlie the difficulties experienced in observing Piwi on its target loci by ChIP (Marinov et al., 2015).
evidence: Speculative explanation supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Panx and Nxf2 are interdependent for their protein stability and proper subcellular localization.
source: We find that Panx and Nxf2 are interdependent for their protein stability and proper subcellular localization
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and western blot data showing mutual dependence.

claim: Correct assembly of the PICTS complex is essential for TGS, while the silencing capacity, per se, resides in Panx.
source: underscoring the fact that correct assembly of the PICTS complex is essential for TGS, while the silencing capacity, per se, resides in Panx.
evidence: Inferred from tethering experiments showing that Panx N-terminus alone can induce silencing.

claim: Previous work reported a partial destabilization of Nxf2 in cells depleted of Nxt1.
source: Of note, previous work reported a partial destabilization of Nxf2 in cells depleted of Nxt1 (Herold et al., 2001), potentially extending the interdependency to all three proteins.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study by Herold et al., 2001.

claim: RIP-seq experiments from unperturbed cells found transposon RNAs enriched only with Panx, but not with Nxf2.
source: RIP-seq experiments from unperturbed cells found transposon RNAs enriched only with Panx, as reported (Sienski et al., 2015), but not with Nxf2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F), possibly due to low substrate availability combined with an insensitive assay.
evidence: Supported by RIP-seq data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F) and citation to previous study.

claim: Another recent report did not detect transposon enrichment in Nxf2 CLIP-seq from wild-type cells.
source: These results are consistent with another recent report that did not detect transposon enrichment in Nxf2 CLIP-seq from wild-type cells (Batki et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Batki et al., 2019.

claim: Two studies identified transposon mRNA association with Nxf2 in CLIP-seq experiments upon depletion of Mael or by using a stable cell line and depletion of endogenous Nxf2.
source: However, two other studies identified transposon mRNA association with Nxf2 in CLIP-seq experiments upon depletion of the previously described TGS factor, Mael (Zhao et al., 2019), or by using a stable cell line and depletion of endogenous Nxf2 (Murano et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Zhao et al., 2019 and Murano et al., 2019.

claim: Nxf2 might be important for stabilizing the binding of Panx to nascent RNAs.
source: Considered together, these data suggest that Nxf2 might be important for stabilizing the binding of Panx to nascent RNAs.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of multiple experimental findings.

claim: Murano and colleagues find that Panx interacts with Nxf2, Piwi, Mael and Arx.
source: Of note, Murano and colleagues find that Panx interacts with Nxf2, Piwi, Mael and Arx (Murano et al., 2019)
evidence: Supported by citation to Murano et al., 2019.

claim: Other TGS factors might come into contact with the PICTS complex, although the relationship between these factors and PICTS requires further investigation.
